name: St. Regis Chicago
positioning: The St. Regis Chicago, a downtown hotel where the Chicago River meets Lake Michigan, in a tower designed by Jeanne Gang
best_for: Food-focused travelers who want Tuscan and Japanese-inspired restaurants under one roof
Spa and fitness lovers who want a heated indoor pool and outdoor sundeck
Families looking for a program built around younger guests

facts.text: The St. Regis Chicago is situated where the Chicago River meets Lake Michigan.
The tower was designed by Jeanne Gang.
Designers Gensler and KTGY Simeone Deary Design drew inspiration from the buildings that followed the Chicago Fire of 1871.
Tre Dita is led by Chef Evan Funke and serves handmade Tuscan pasta and dishes prepared on a woodfire grill.
Tre Dita is Italian for 'three fingers', a nod to the measurement of bistecca Fiorentina.
Rooms have private marble bathrooms with rainfall showers.
Every room comes with one of four types of soaking tubs.
The St. Regis Spa has a Celebration Bar and an Iridium Lounge.
The fitness facility has a heated indoor swimming pool, an outdoor pool sundeck and a yoga studio.
The Family Traditions program offers activities and experiences tailored to younger guests and their families.

highlights.text: The St. Regis Chicago is in the tallest building in the world designed by a female architect.
Tre Dita is designated as the first certified Tuscan restaurant in the United States.
Miru, on the 11th floor, offers all-day dining and Japanese-inspired dishes with two outdoor terraces, led by Chef Hisanobu Osaka.
The hotel's Bloody Mary, The 1871, is a tribute to the Great Chicago Fire and uses a local rye whiskey.
The hotel's arrival esplanade connects openly with Lakeshore East Park, a 6-acre development with green space and ornamental water gardens.

considerations.text: St. Regis Butler Service is available exclusively for suite accommodations.
Lakeshore East, between the hotel and Lake Michigan, is a quiet residential area.
The minimum age to check in is 21.
